rationale: After the alcohol withdrawal timeline block, tests application of the thiamine-before-glucose rule and correct recognition of Wernicke risk — a classic PS3.1 clinical emergency trap.

After the diagnostic criteria and CAGE screening block, tests understanding of the ICD-11 distinction between harmful use and dependence — a well-documented PS3.1 examination trap where students conflate the two.

After the opioid use disorder management block, tests correct first-line pharmacotherapy selection for nicotine dependence — distinguishing varenicline, NRT, and bupropion, a common PS3.1 prescribing question.
